build_dlc: Pull in APPID from /etc/lsb-release Nebraska needs appid being present in DLC (and platform) payload's json file. We need the appid of the platform image in order to build the appid of the DLC. This CL grabs the CHROMEOS_RELEASE_APPID of the platform image and concatenate it with the dlc id in order to create the DLC appid. This way, the paygen can later extract the appid from the /etc/lsb-release of the input image file (DLC or platform) and dump them to the payload's json file. More unittests added. BUG=chromium:913076 TEST=unittests TEST=emerge-edgar dummy-dlc; and mounted the image, the etc/lsb-release had the correct key-value parameters. shill: wifi: return WiFiEndpointRefPtr instead of WiFiEndpoint pointer All current callers of WiFiEndpoint::MakeEndpoint() and WiFiEndpoint::MakeOpenEndpoint() capture the newly constructed WiFiEndpoint object into a WiFiEndpointRefPtr. This CL changes both methods to return a WiFiEndpointRefPtr instead of bare WiFiEndpoint pointer to prevent a potential situation where a caller captures the newly constructed WiFiEndpoint by a bare WiFiEndpoint pointer and forgets to destroy it. BUG=None TEST=Run unit tests. chromeos-fonts: Unmount cache before bind mounting If fc-cache fails during emerge, the ebuild leaves ${ROOT}/usr/share/cache/fontconfig mounted. The retry then mounts on top of it and generates the cache files. When the retry unmounts the directory, it ends up restoring the original empty cache output, so the build fails again. To avoid this: 1. Run fc-cache in a subshell and unmount even if it fails. 2. Check for an already mounted fontconfig and unmount it first. BUG=None TEST=emerge-grunt chromeos-fonts Change-Id: Iedddd70d5c40090818f5e0c96be8bc2cf464c3cd Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1495772 Commit-Ready: Benjamin Gordon <bmgordon@chromium.org> Tested-by: Benjamin Gordon <bmgordon@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>
